I would give every person on the planet access to free, high-quality, lifelong education—education that teaches not only literacy, numeracy, science and the arts, but also critical thinking, empathy, and practical skills for modern life.

Why that one change?

1. Multiplier effect  
   • Health: Educated people make better health choices, reduce disease spread, and lower infant mortality.  
   • Economy: Skills drive innovation, productivity, and better jobs, shrinking the wealth gap.  
   • Environment: Understanding ecosystems and climate science builds public will for sustainable policies.  
   • Peace & governance: Critical thinking and media literacy make societies more resilient to demagoguery and misinformation, reducing conflict and strengthening democracy.  

2. Human dignity and autonomy  
   The ability to read, question, and learn continuously is the gateway to full participation in society. It empowers individuals to shape their own lives rather than be shaped by circumstance.

How might it be implemented?

• Universal connectivity: Treat broadband like a public utility; combine satellite, fiber, and community networks to reach remote areas.  
• Open educational resources in every major language: Curate textbooks, coursework, and vocational modules that anyone can download, remix, and share.  
• Teacher development and status: Pay teachers professional salaries, provide ongoing training, and elevate the profession’s social standing.  
• Blended learning hubs: Pair online content with local mentors, makerspaces, and laboratories so learning is hands-on, culturally relevant, and socially connected.  
• Early-childhood to adulthood: Offer free preschool, compulsory basic schooling, and modular micro-credentials throughout life so workers can reskill as technology changes.  
• Focus on empathy & civics: Integrate service projects, cross-cultural exchanges, and deliberative forums into curricula to practice cooperation and ethical reasoning.

What would the world look like afterward?

• Extreme poverty falls sharply as people create and fill higher-value jobs.  
• Fewer wars and genocides, because populations are harder to manipulate with propaganda.  
• Technological breakthroughs accelerate, but with stronger ethical safeguards.  
• Green technologies scale faster, carbon emissions drop, and biodiversity loss slows.  
• Social mobility improves, reducing resentment and polarisation.  
• Billions of individual stories—artists, scientists, caregivers, entrepreneurs—unfold that would otherwise have remained untold.

In short, unlocking every mind through universal, holistic education doesn’t solve every problem outright, but it supplies humanity with the cognitive and moral tools to tackle all the others together.
